activities.label: Screening teasers and CIMs
activities.solution: Read each inbound teaser or CIM, score it against your investment criteria, and produce a one-page summary with the reasons to pass or proceed.
activities.first_step: Write your investment criteria as explicit pass and proceed rules.
activities.check: A deal professional reviews every pass close to the line and samples clear passes each week.
activities.check_ai: Load CIMs only into tools your NDAs and whoever leads compliance allow.

activities.label: Building market maps and target lists
activities.solution: Build and refresh target lists from licensed databases and public filings, with each company tagged by sub-sector, size indicators, and ownership.
activities.first_step: Choose one sector and compare a generated list with the best list your team has built by hand.
activities.check: A deal professional confirms each shortlisted name before anyone acts on it.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Choose one sector, and write down how your best target list was built.
activities.check_ai: Check that your data licenses allow this use before loading licensed data into any AI tool.

activities.label: Logging deals and contacts in the CRM
activities.solution: Draft CRM entries for deals, intermediaries, and meetings from the deal inbox and calendar, and flag duplicates. A person confirms each entry before it goes in.
activities.first_step: Choose one shared deal inbox as a test, and list what is entered by hand today.
activities.check: Keep private meetings out of this by rule.

activities.label: Tracking intermediary coverage and follow-ups
activities.solution: Watch CRM and email for contacts going cold, then draft a follow-up with relevant context for the deal owner to approve.
activities.first_step: Agree who counts as a priority intermediary and how long is too long without contact.
activities.check: The relationship owner approves every message. Nothing goes out unreviewed.

activities.label: Reviewing data room documents
activities.solution: Index the data room documents your access terms allow you to process, extract key terms and figures with citations to the source page, and flag gaps against your checklist.
activities.first_step: Choose one closed deal as a test, and write down what the team actually found on it.
activities.check: Keep clean team and privileged material out of general review. The deal team checks anything that reaches a memo against the document itself.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Choose one closed deal, and write down what the team actually found in the data room.
activities.process_solution: Agree a standard checklist for data room review, and record what each review found.
activities.check_ai: Check the NDA and data room rules before loading anything into a tool. Every extracted fact links to its page, and the deal team opens the page for anything that reaches a memo.

activities.label: Managing request lists and trackers
activities.solution: Match data room uploads to open requests, update the tracker, and produce a daily list of what is missing and from whom.
activities.first_step: Build one request list template across the workstreams from the lists on your last deal.
activities.check: The deal lead confirms an item is complete before it closes on the tracker.

activities.label: Summarizing expert and customer calls
activities.solution: Turn call transcripts into structured notes by theme, showing where sources agree and disagree, with quotes to back each point.
activities.first_step: Agree a standard note format, then, in a tool whoever leads compliance has approved, process the calls from one closed deal.
activities.check: Confirm recording consent and expert network rules first. If a call may contain confidential or material non-public information, stop and send it to compliance before it is summarized or shared. Verify quotes before reuse.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Agree a standard note format, and use it for the calls on your next deal.

activities.label: Spreading financials into models
activities.solution: Pull figures from management accounts and CIMs into your model template, mapped to your line items, with each number traceable to its source.
activities.first_step: Fix one template and mapping, then spread three past sets of accounts with different formats by hand and note where the mapping breaks.
activities.check: A person on the deal team ties totals back to source. The model structure and assumptions stay with the team.
activities.check_ai: Load CIMs and management accounts only into tools your NDAs and whoever leads compliance allow.

activities.label: Drafting IC memos
activities.solution: Produce a first draft in your house format from diligence notes and the model, with each claim linked to its source, for the team to edit.
activities.first_step: Collect five memos you consider excellent and turn their shared structure into the template.
activities.check: The deal team owns the argument and the recommendation, and ties every figure to its source before the memo circulates.
activities.process_solution: Agree one memo template and one review path, so that drafts stop being rebuilt from scratch.
activities.check_ai: Keep this within tools approved for firm data.

activities.label: Finding past deals and precedents
activities.solution: Search past memos, models, and IC notes in plain language, with answers that cite the original document and respect access rights.
activities.first_step: Gather the memos from your last fund, with permissions matching who can see them today.
activities.check: Access rights must carry over, including any information barriers.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: List where memos from your last fund are kept, and who can see them today.

activities.label: Assembling packs, minutes, and actions
activities.solution: Assemble the pack from approved versions, circulate it, and track actions until they close. A person keeps the minutes.
activities.first_step: Define one folder and naming standard that marks which version is final.
activities.check: Whoever chairs the meeting approves the minutes, as they form part of the firm's record.

activities.label: The investment decision itself
activities.solution: Keep the decision with the committee. AI can prepare a challenge list of open risks and past comparable deals beforehand.
activities.first_step: Add a short list of counterarguments to the next IC pack and ask members whether it helped.
activities.check: Responsibility for the decision stays with the committee.

activities.label: Preparing the pipeline review
activities.solution: Assemble the pipeline review from the deal tracker and recent notes, and draft a short status for each active deal.
activities.first_step: Agree the five fields every active deal must show in the review.
activities.check: Deal leads confirm each status before the meeting.
activities.check_ai: Keep the draft within tools approved for deal information.

activities.label: Comparing NDAs and deal documents
activities.solution: Compare incoming drafts with your standard positions and past deals, and list the deviations for counsel with suggested fallback wording.
activities.first_step: Start with NDAs: write down your standard positions.
activities.check: Counsel reviews all output. This supports the legal review and does not replace it.

activities.label: Running closing checklists
activities.solution: Keep the closing checklist current from email and signature platforms, and chase owners for outstanding items.
activities.first_step: Build one checklist format from your last closing, with a named owner for each item.
activities.check: Counsel and the deal lead sign off on conditions before they are marked complete, and a person sends any chase outside the firm.

activities.label: Handing deals over after close
activities.solution: Build the post-close record from the memo, model, and final documents: key terms, covenants, reporting duties, and the 100-day plan's owners and dates.
activities.first_step: Define what whoever runs the investment after close needs on day one, then build it by hand once from a recent deal.
activities.check: The deal lead and whoever takes over the investment both confirm covenant dates and reporting duties.

activities.label: Negotiating terms
activities.solution: Keep negotiation with your team and counsel. AI can prepare an issues list and show what you accepted on past deals.
activities.first_step: Build a simple record of positions you accepted on recent deals.
activities.check: Keep counterparty and privileged material within approved tools.

activities.label: Tracking adviser engagements and deal costs
activities.solution: Log every adviser engagement, budget, and invoice in one place, and flag spend against budget and broken-deal costs.
activities.first_step: List the adviser engagements on your last two deals, with budget and final cost.
activities.check: Whoever leads finance approves how costs are allocated between the firm, its funds, and any co-investors, under your LPA.

activities.label: Chasing portcos for KPI files
activities.solution: Request files on schedule, chase late ones, check they arrived complete, and load them into your portfolio model, with exceptions sent to one owner.
activities.first_step: Agree one KPI template and due date with two portfolio companies.
activities.check: A person approves the reminder wording in advance, and handles exceptions and any other message to company management.
activities.process_solution: Agree one KPI template and one due date with a few companies first. Automate reminders and completeness checks once that holds.

activities.label: Standardizing KPI data across portcos
activities.solution: Map each company's accounts to your standard definitions with reusable rules, and flag values that break the pattern instead of passing them on.
activities.first_step: Write down definitions for your ten most-used KPIs, and check whether each company uses them the same way.
activities.check: Anyone changing a mapping leaves a record, and reported figures reconcile to company accounts.
activities.process_solution: Write one set of KPI definitions, map each company's accounts to them, and flag values that break the pattern.

activities.label: Writing variance commentary
activities.solution: Draft explanations of movement against budget and prior year from the numbers and management commentary, marking anything unexplained as a question.
activities.first_step: Choose one company as a test, and keep its latest commentary to compare against.
activities.check: The person who leads the investment edits and signs off, and causes the data does not support must be marked as unexplained.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Choose one company, and write down which variances your readers actually use.
activities.check_ai: Keep this within tools approved for firm data.

activities.label: Spotting underperformance early
activities.solution: Check every new data point against budget, covenant headroom, and trend rules, and send an alert with context to the owner.
activities.first_step: Agree three warning rules with the people who lead each investment.
activities.check: Review false alarms and missed warnings monthly, and adjust the rules with the people who receive them. The lead on each investment stays responsible for tracking covenants.

activities.label: Digesting board packs
activities.solution: Summarize each pack against the last one: what changed, what is missing, and where the numbers and narrative disagree.
activities.first_step: Using only a tool approved for firm data, try it on your last two packs from one company and ask the director what was missed.
activities.check: Directors read the full pack. The summary only points to what changed. Board materials stay within approved tools, and packs from listed companies go to compliance first.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Ask a director which parts of the last pack they actually read, and which they skipped.

activities.label: Preparing questions for the board
activities.solution: Prepare a question list from the pack, open actions, and the investment case, linked to the page behind each question.
activities.first_step: In a tool approved for firm data, prepare questions from the last pack for one company and ask the director which ones they would have kept.
activities.check: The director chooses what to raise and how, because these are relationship decisions. Board materials stay within approved tools, and packs from listed companies go to compliance first.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Ask a director which questions from the last meeting mattered most, and why.

activities.label: Tracking board actions
activities.solution: Extract actions from minutes into one tracker with owners and dates, and bring overdue items into the next pack.
activities.first_step: Move actions from one portfolio company into a shared tracker.
activities.check: The company secretary or director confirms the wording of each action.

activities.label: Board-level judgment and decisions
activities.solution: Keep these decisions with directors. AI can prepare the background.
activities.first_step: List which board decisions recur, and what evidence directors want before them.
activities.check: Directors stay responsible for these decisions.

activities.label: Tracking covenants and reporting duties
activities.solution: Keep every covenant test and reporting duty in one calendar, calculate the routine tests from reported figures as an early check, not as the company's certificate, and alert the responsible person before a date is missed.
activities.first_step: List the covenant tests and reporting dates for one investment in a single table.
activities.check: The person responsible for the investment confirms each test result, and counsel reviews any possible breach.

activities.label: Tracking value creation plans
activities.solution: Keep 100-day and value creation plans current from company updates, link each initiative to its KPI, and draft status reports for owners to confirm.
activities.first_step: Put one company's plan in a shared format, with a measurable KPI on every initiative.
activities.check: Initiative owners confirm status. Status must not be inferred from silence.
activities.process_solution: Put every plan in one shared tracker, with an owner, a date, and a measurable KPI for each initiative, before adding any AI.

activities.label: Reusing what worked across portcos
activities.solution: Make past plans, operating reviews, and results searchable, so a new company can start from what worked in similar situations.
activities.first_step: Write up five past initiatives with their results in a single format.
activities.check: Check for sensitive company data before sharing anything between portfolio companies, and ask counsel first if they compete.
activities.check_ai: Keep this within tools approved for firm data.

activities.label: Benchmarking portcos
activities.solution: Compare companies with each other and with licensed external data on standardized metrics, and highlight the gaps worth a conversation.
activities.first_step: Pick five comparable metrics and benchmark two similar companies.
activities.check: Confirm definitions match before comparing. Keep company-level results inside the firm, check your data license, and ask counsel before sharing anything between companies that compete.

activities.label: Coaching management teams
activities.solution: Keep this with the people who coach your management teams. AI can help with their preparation and follow-up notes.
activities.first_step: Ask them which preparation takes the most time before a management session.
activities.check: Management teams should know how any meeting notes are stored and used.

activities.label: Tracking add-on targets for portfolio companies
activities.solution: Keep one list of add-on targets per platform company, with the last contact and next step for each, and flag stalled conversations.
activities.first_step: Put the current add-on targets for one platform company in one list, with an owner and a next step.
activities.check: The deal lead decides whom to approach. Keep it out of shared tools if your NDAs or data licenses do not allow it.

activities.label: Preparing exit data and history
activities.solution: Assemble the performance history, KPI bridges, and sell-side or vendor diligence inputs from your portfolio data, and flag gaps early.
activities.first_step: Choose one company and list what an exit readiness check should cover.
activities.check: Finance and advisers verify anything that may enter sale documents.
activities.process_solution: Keep one exit data file for each investment, tied to the accounts, and record the gaps as you find them.

activities.label: Drafting sale materials
activities.solution: Produce first drafts of the equity story and management presentation sections from board packs and plans, with sources marked. Start this after the exit data is ready.
activities.first_step: In a tool approved for firm data, draft one section from a past exit and compare it with the final document.
activities.check: Advisers and counsel review all statements before use.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Take a past exit, and list which sections of the sale materials were rebuilt from scratch.

activities.label: Building buyer lists
activities.solution: Build strategic and financial buyer lists with the rationale for each, using recent deals and stated strategies.
activities.first_step: Compare a generated list with the buyer list from a recent process.
activities.check: The deal team and adviser decide who is approached, and handle confidentiality. Check that your data licenses allow this use.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Take a recent process, and write down how its buyer list was built.

activities.label: Deciding exit timing and route
activities.solution: Keep the decision with partners. AI can keep market comparables and readiness data ready for that discussion.
activities.first_step: Define what an exit review for each company should contain.
activities.check: Partners own the decision. Conflicts, such as a sale to another fund or a continuation vehicle, go to compliance, counsel, and the LPAC as the LPA requires.

activities.label: Preparing partial exits and continuation options
activities.solution: Assemble the performance history and terms that each exit route needs, and draft a neutral comparison for the partners to review.
activities.first_step: List what you would need to show for one investment closest to exit, under each route you might consider.
activities.check: Partners and counsel decide the route, and any conflict of interest goes to compliance, counsel, and the LPAC as the LPA requires.

activities.label: Drafting quarterly LP letters
activities.solution: Draft fund and portfolio commentary from approved numbers and last quarter's letter, in your house voice, with every figure tied to its source.
activities.first_step: In a tool approved for firm data, generate last quarter's letter from last quarter's inputs and have a partner mark up the differences.
activities.check: IR, finance, compliance, and a partner approve the letter. Every figure must tie to the books.
activities.process_solution: Separate what your LPA and investors require from what is optional, reuse standard wording only where nothing has changed, and have a partner decide what optional content to drop.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Mark up last quarter's letter, separating what repeats from what needs a partner's view.

activities.label: Filling ILPA and LP-specific templates
activities.solution: Fill ILPA and investor-specific templates from one approved dataset, or check the administrator's version against it, and run tie-out checks before review.
activities.first_step: List every template you produce, note which ILPA version each fund uses, and mark where they request the same data.
activities.check: Finance signs off the source dataset, and exceptions are reviewed by a person.
activities.process_solution: List which templates an LPA, side letter, or investor request requires, and have whoever owns LP reporting approve retiring any other.

activities.label: Merging data from portcos and the administrator
activities.solution: Combine administrator, portfolio, and valuation data into one quarter-end dataset, reconcile it, and send breaks to named owners.
activities.first_step: Map the data flow for one quarter and note where it is copied by hand.
activities.check: Reconciliation breaks need a person to resolve them, with a record of why. Finance signs off the merged figures.
activities.process_solution: Agree one data cut-off and one source for each line of the report, and remove manual merging where you can.

activities.label: Uploading to portals and distributing
activities.solution: Publish approved documents to the right investor folders with access checks and a delivery record.
activities.first_step: Check that your record of which investor receives which document is correct.
activities.check: Before each release, a person checks the full list of which investor receives which document and approves it. A spot-check is not enough for investor-specific documents such as capital account statements.

activities.label: Answering DDQs and RFPs
activities.solution: Build an approved answer library and draft each new DDQ from it, with citations and a flag on anything stale or unanswered.
activities.first_step: Put your last three completed DDQs in one document and mark which answers remain approved.
activities.check: IR and compliance approve answers, because these are representations to investors.
activities.process_solution: Keep one approved library of past answers, with an owner and a review date for each, and reuse it.

activities.label: Handling ad hoc LP questions
activities.solution: Classify each incoming question, gather the data and past answers, and draft a reply for IR to review.
activities.first_step: List last quarter's LP questions to find which types recur.
activities.check: IR reviews and sends every reply. Whoever leads compliance reviews any reply that gives information not already given to all investors, or that draws on another investor's question or data.

activities.label: Completing annual ESG and LP questionnaires
activities.solution: Pre-fill annual ESG and investor surveys from portfolio data and last year's answers, and show what changed.
activities.first_step: Combine last year's surveys and find the overlap between them.
activities.check: The owner checks the evidence and signs off all figures, and compliance reviews anything stated to investors.

activities.label: Sensitive LP conversations and meetings
activities.solution: Keep these conversations with partners and IR. AI can prepare a short brief on the investor's history and open points.
activities.first_step: Decide what a good pre-call brief includes for your top ten LPs.
activities.check: A partner decides what is said and sent, and the brief contains nothing about any other investor. Whoever leads compliance reviews anything that gives this investor information not already given to all investors.

activities.label: Collecting ESG data for reports
activities.solution: Send one standard ESG data request to each company, check answers against last year's, and flag gaps.
activities.first_step: List the ESG fields you report, note which an LP, side letter, or regulation requires, and mark the rest for review.
activities.check: Whoever signs off ESG reporting reviews any figure that changed sharply, and any public claim or statement to investors goes through compliance.

activities.label: Refreshing pitch decks and PPM sections
activities.solution: Update decks, PPM sections, and the data room from approved data, and keep figures, case studies, and wording consistent across documents.
activities.first_step: Create a single approved source for your key figures and case studies.
activities.check: Compliance and counsel review all marketing materials under the rules that apply to you, including how case studies are chosen and how gross and net returns are shown. Check that every data room file is current and cleared for each investor.

activities.label: Building track record tables
activities.solution: Generate track record and attribution tables from one reconciled dataset tied to audited fund financials, with checks that every version ties out.
activities.first_step: Rebuild the track record for three deals in one fund from source and record each difference.
activities.check: Finance and compliance verify the method and every published figure, including how gross and net returns are shown under the rules that apply to you.
activities.process_solution: Keep one source file for the track record, tied to fund records, and archive other copies rather than delete them.

activities.label: Processing subscription documents and investor checks
activities.solution: Check subscription documents for missing or inconsistent items, track each investor's status to closing, and list open KYC and AML items for the owner.
activities.first_step: List what was checked for each investor at your last close, and where it got stuck.
activities.check: Compliance, with the administrator or counsel, clears every investor. No tool accepts an investor or clears a sanctions or KYC match. Keep identity documents and personal data only in tools approved for that data.

activities.label: Identifying and prioritizing LPs
activities.solution: Rank prospective LPs on mandate fit, past commitments, and relationships, using licensed data and the CRM, with the reasoning shown.
activities.first_step: In a tool approved for firm data, test the ranking against the investors who committed to your last fund.
activities.check: IR decides who is approached and follows the marketing rules for each jurisdiction. Check that your data licenses allow this use.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Take the investors who committed to your last fund, and write down what they had in common.

activities.label: Keeping LP records in the CRM current
activities.solution: Update LP contacts and interaction history from email and calendar, flag duplicates and departures, and take commitment amounts only from the official investor records.
activities.first_step: Clean the top 50 LP records and define what must always be current.
activities.check: Follow data privacy rules on what is captured, and sample records weekly at first.

activities.label: Writing up LP meetings
activities.solution: Turn meeting notes or approved recordings into a structured summary with next steps, filed against the investor.
activities.first_step: Agree a one-page note format and use it for one month.
activities.check: Get consent for recordings, and the meeting owner approves the note.

activities.label: Tracking investor follow-ups
activities.solution: Track promised follow-ups across email and CRM, remind owners, and draft replies with the right materials attached.
activities.first_step: Start with one list of open commitments from your last ten LP meetings.
activities.check: The owner approves every outbound message and confirms each attachment is cleared for that investor.

activities.label: Preparing LPAC and annual meetings
activities.solution: Draft the agenda, pack, and minutes from approved materials, track the consents and votes the LPA requires, and keep the record of each decision.
activities.first_step: List every LPAC consent and annual meeting item from the last two years, with the LPA clause behind each one.
activities.check: Counsel and whoever leads compliance review every conflict or consent item, and a partner approves what goes to LPAC members.

activities.label: Preparing and reconciling capital calls and distributions
activities.solution: Calculate or check each investor's share from commitments and LPA terms, draft the notices for finance to approve, match notices to bank movements, and send the breaks to a person.
activities.first_step: Measure how many items match automatically on last quarter's calls using simple rules.
activities.check: Finance approves every notice and allocation, including excused investors, later-close adjustments, and the distribution waterfall. Payment approvals should have two-person sign-off, separate from this work. A missed payment goes to whoever leads finance and to counsel, because the LPA may set default terms.
activities.process_solution: Standardize the notice and the reconciliation, and remove retyping, before spending anything on them. Payment approvals should have two-person sign-off.

activities.label: Checking fee and carry calculations
activities.solution: Recalculate fees and carry independently from LPA terms and side letters, and flag differences from the figures your administrator or finance team produced.
activities.first_step: Write down one fund's fee terms in a form a calculation can follow.
activities.check: Finance reviews all differences before anything changes, and counsel interprets any unclear LPA or side letter term.
activities.process_solution: Write down one fund's fee and carry terms, keep one calculation file per fund, compare it with the figures your administrator or finance team produced, and archive other internal copies rather than delete them.

activities.label: Reviewing administrator reports and supporting the audit
activities.solution: Check administrator packs against your own records, list breaks and unusual movements for review, and keep the auditor's request list current with each item's owner and status.
activities.first_step: List the checks your team runs each close, and the items the auditor requested last year.
activities.check: Whoever leads finance signs off, the review leaves an audit trail, and a person in finance sends everything that goes to the auditor.
activities.process_solution: List what is re-checked each quarter and which breaks recur, fix the cause of those breaks with your administrator, and have whoever leads finance approve any change to the checks.

activities.label: Valuation judgments
activities.solution: Keep the judgment with the people who set your marks. AI can compile comparables, prior marks, and policy references.
activities.first_step: Write down who sets each mark, who challenges it, and where the reason is recorded.
activities.check: Whoever sets each mark records why under any valuation policy, and the deal team does not set its own mark alone.

activities.label: Assembling the quarterly valuation pack
activities.solution: Pull last quarter's marks, KPIs, and comparable data into one standard pack for each investment, and flag what changed. People still decide every mark.
activities.first_step: List what went into last quarter's valuation pack for one investment, and agree a one-page standard format.
activities.check: The people who set your marks decide every mark, and the pack does not propose a value. Check that your data licenses allow this use.
activities.process_solution: List what each valuation pack contains, remove only what neither the people who set marks nor the auditor uses, and agree one format.

activities.label: Tracking side letter and LPA obligations
activities.solution: Extract obligations, restrictions, and MFN elections from LPAs and side letters into a register, with dates, owners, and a link to the clause.
activities.first_step: Start the register for one fund, and ask counsel to check a sample.
activities.check: Counsel validates interpretations. The register points to clauses and does not replace them. Load side letters only into tools approved for them, and limit who can see each investor's terms.
activities.process_solution: Put every side letter and LPA obligation in one register, with an owner and a date for each, before adding any AI.

activities.label: Preparing regulatory filings
activities.solution: Gather data for recurring filings such as Form ADV, Form PF, Form D, or AIFMD Annex IV reporting, validate it, and show changes since the last filing.
activities.first_step: Map each field of one filing to its data source.
activities.check: Compliance and whoever signs for the firm review and submit every filing.
activities.process_solution: Map each field to its source, remove manual re-keying, and add a second check before filing.

activities.label: Running the compliance calendar, attestations, and restricted list
activities.solution: Schedule attestations, personal trading and gift declarations, restricted list updates, and the annual compliance review, chase responses, and keep the record for exams.
activities.first_step: Put all recurring compliance tasks on one calendar with one owner.
activities.check: Whoever leads compliance reviews exceptions and conflicts and decides every restricted list change.

activities.label: Compliance judgment calls
activities.solution: Keep decisions with whoever leads compliance and counsel. AI can surface the relevant policy and past decisions.
activities.first_step: Create a searchable log of past compliance decisions.
activities.check: They stay responsible for the decision, and counsel decides whether privileged advice goes in the log.

activities.label: Responding to regulator and exam requests
activities.solution: Find the records a request asks for, draft an index, and track what has been provided and when.
activities.first_step: List the records your last regulatory request asked for, or if you have had none, the records you must keep, and where each one sits.
activities.check: Whoever leads compliance and counsel approve everything before it is sent, and counsel reviews for privileged material. Keep this work within approved tools.

activities.label: Finding documents and past work
activities.solution: Offer plain-language search across shared drives, with cited answers and existing permissions respected. Leave email archives out unless compliance and counsel agree.
activities.first_step: Clean up one high-value folder, then write down ten real questions from your team and check whether your current search finds the answers.
activities.check: Review permissions first, because search shows people whatever they can already access. Test that information barriers and privileged folders hold before wider use.

activities.label: Capturing know-how from senior people
activities.solution: Turn recurring partner guidance into playbooks through short interviews and existing documents, then keep them searchable.
activities.first_step: Record one 30-minute interview on the question juniors most often ask.
activities.check: The senior expert reviews each playbook, and it carries an owner and a review date.

activities.label: Onboarding new team members
activities.solution: Give new joiners a guide built from your templates and past work that answers routine questions with sources.
activities.first_step: List the 20 questions that new analysts ask most in their first month.
activities.check: Assign an owner to keep the source material current, and include only material every new joiner may see.

activities.label: Producing internal market research
activities.solution: Produce regular sector briefings from licensed and public sources, with citations and a note on what changed.
activities.first_step: Replace one recurring sector update and ask its readers if it holds up.
activities.check: Show sources to readers, and follow your data licensing terms.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: Ask readers of one recurring sector update which parts they actually use.

activities.label: Processing expenses and invoices
activities.solution: Read invoices and receipts, code them to the right fund or the management company, and route exceptions for approval.
activities.first_step: Write down your rules for allocating expenses between funds and the management company.
activities.check: Finance reviews every fund-versus-manager allocation against the LPA and any written policy, and payment approvals stay with people.
activities.process_solution: Agree one coding guide and one approval path for expenses and invoices, and remove duplicate entry.

activities.label: Reviewing software and AI vendors
activities.solution: Keep one register of software and AI vendors, draft each review from the contract and security answers, and flag changes to data use, retention, and who can see your data.
activities.first_step: List every AI tool in use today, including individual accounts, and what firm data has gone into each.
activities.check: Whoever leads compliance and whoever runs operations approve each tool before firm data goes in, and a person reads the contract terms on confidentiality and model training.
activities.first_step_if_no_ai: List the software that holds firm data, and who approved it.

activities.label: Scheduling and meeting preparation
activities.solution: Prepare meeting briefs from CRM, email, and files, handle routine scheduling including interviews, and draft follow-up lists for approval.
activities.first_step: Agree with one partner what a useful daily brief would contain.
activities.check: Assistants or owners approve anything that goes out, and calendar access is controlled.

activities.label: Handling IT and access requests
activities.solution: Handle routine requests and joiner and leaver steps through one request form, with approvals recorded.
activities.first_step: Create a joiner and leaver checklist covering every system.
activities.check: Access changes need named approval and periodic review.

activities.label: Covenant waivers and workouts
activities.solution: Keep the decision with the partners and credit leads who own it. AI can compile the covenant terms, history, and correspondence.
activities.first_step: Write down who decides a waiver or workout, and where the reason is recorded.
activities.check: The deal lead and whoever leads compliance record each decision and why.
